title: Distinct valvometry signal patterns associated with spawning and fecal ejection in the mussel Mytilus galloprovincialis
content:
Abstract

Spain is the largest European producer of mussels for human consumption, and this production depends heavily on mussel seed availability. However, multiple environmental factors make it difficult to accurately predict the timing for deploying seed-collector ropes, posing a challenge in seed supply and production management. New tools are therefore being explored to help anticipate spawning events in mussels. In this work, a cost-effective High-Frequency Non-Invasive (HFNI) valvometry apparatus based on Hall-effect sensors was used to explore spawning-related valve-movement patterns in Mytilus galloprovincialis. Spawning produced distinct zig-zag-shaped spikes spaced by approximately 10–20 min. A total of 12 mussels spawned during the study, and this waveform was consistently observed across all spawning individuals. Based on these patterns, a preliminary detection protocol for a biological early warning system (BEWS) was developed using periodicity as the main detection criterion, achieving a sensitivity of 0.75 and a precision of 0.25. Video inspection showed that false positives corresponded to fecal-pellet ejection, which generated characteristic M- and W-shaped waveforms. These findings suggest the importance of waveform shape as a behavioral marker in mussel valvometry, providing a basis for future improvements in mussel-based biosensors.
